summary: Static verification of E1's 'Smart Refresh Sound' feature on both /app/frontend (PartnerApp) and /app/Customer. Scope: playRefreshFeedback() wiring in both RefreshNote.tsx files, new refresh-tick.wav asset validity, require path resolution, web crash safety, and package manifest presence of expo-audio/expo-haptics. Verified via `python wave` on both WAV assets, `npx tsc --noEmit` on PartnerApp, `npx eslint` on both RefreshNote files, and manual logic review.

static_review_findings.wav_assets: Both Customer/assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav and frontend/assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav are valid: WAV, mono, 44100 Hz, 16-bit (sampwidth=2), 3969 frames = 90.0 ms. Files are byte-identical in size (7982 bytes). Matches spec (~90ms, 44.1kHz mono 16-bit).
static_review_findings.require_path: `require('../../assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav')` from src/components/RefreshNote.tsx resolves to <app-root>/assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav. Confirmed file present at /app/frontend/assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav and /app/Customer/assets/sounds/refresh-tick.wav.
static_review_findings.package_manifests: Both frontend/package.json and Customer/package.json declare expo-audio ~57.0.5 and expo-haptics ~57.0.3. PartnerApp node_modules confirms expo-audio and expo-haptics installed.
static_review_findings.RefreshNote.tsx (both apps, identical): playRefreshFeedback() correctly: (1) fires Haptics.impactAsync(Light) with .catch(() => {}) so a rejected promise never surfaces as an unhandled rejection; (2) early-returns on Platform.OS==='web' BEFORE touching expo-audio (so native-only expo-audio require is never evaluated on web — safe); (3) wraps the entire native branch in try/catch so a missing/mis-shimmed expo-audio module cannot crash the host; (4) lazy-creates a single module-level `tickPlayer` via `AA.createAudioPlayer(require(...wav))` and reuses it; (5) wraps `tickPlayer.volume = 0.35` in its own try/catch (volume setter can throw on some backends); (6) calls `tickPlayer.seekTo?.(0)` optionally then `.play()`. The seekTo-before-play pattern allows the player to replay from the start on repeated refreshes (expo-audio keeps lastPosition). Called inside RefreshNoteHost's listener BEFORE setShow(true) and before the spring animation starts, so audio+haptic+visual fire in the same frame → feels synchronous and 'satisfying' as requested.
static_review_findings.web_safety: Platform.OS==='web' branch returns BEFORE `require('expo-audio')` runs, so Metro web bundler never has to resolve the native-only module path at runtime. Haptics on web: expo-haptics is a web-safe no-op in SDK 57; the .catch() still protects against any rejection.
static_review_findings.idempotency / replay: tickPlayer is module-scoped — correct for the single mounted RefreshNoteHost. Multiple rapid refreshes will seekTo(0) then play(), replaying from the start as intended.

tsc_results: PartnerApp: 24 errors (unchanged vs iter_250 baseline). None reference RefreshNote.tsx, refresh-tick, expo-audio, or expo-haptics. Customer: node_modules not installed in this pod → tsc unavailable; code is identical to PartnerApp RefreshNote.tsx (diffed line-for-line).
eslint_results: RefreshNote.tsx: 0 errors, 10 warnings. All 10 warnings are the pre-existing react-hooks/refs false-positives on `a.interpolate(...)` inside the Animated.View style — standard RN Animated API pattern, not real bugs (same as iter_250). No new warnings introduced by playRefreshFeedback.
critical_code_review_comments: Nit: `let tickPlayer: any = null;` with `require('expo-audio')` inside the function body means the player is lazily created on first refresh (good) but is never released. expo-audio players hold a native audio-session resource; for a single ~90ms sfx this is negligible, but on fast-refresh / hot-reload during development you can accumulate zombie players because the module-level var is captured by the stale closure. Not user-visible in production. If E1 wants to be strict, expose a dispose() in a useEffect cleanup on RefreshNoteHost unmount.
Nit: `tickPlayer.volume = 0.35` is set only on first-create. If some future caller mutates volume elsewhere it would persist — currently fine since this is the sole caller.

Nit: The haptic uses ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light which, combined with a 90ms tick, is correctly subtle. On Android some devices map Light to a very weak vibration that's imperceptible — acceptable for 'light vibration' per the requirement wording.

Nit (web): Though web returns before expo-audio require, Metro's web resolver still has to statically see the require call. expo-audio ships a web shim in SDK 57, so this is fine; just noting that if the shim is ever removed, the branch guard is still correct at runtime.

Nit: No user preference / mute toggle. Users on silent mode: iOS respects silent-switch for AVAudioSession ambient category (default in expo-audio) — tick will be muted automatically on iOS silent. Android ignores silent mode for media playback — tick WILL play even on silent. If this is undesirable, consider Haptics-only on Android or add a user setting. Comment '(respects the phone's silent mode on iOS)' in the code is accurate but doesn't mention Android behavior.
test_credentials: n/a — native Expo apps, cannot runtime-test in this pod (Customer has no node_modules; no Expo dev server).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Smart Refresh Sound feature is logic-verified and asset-verified. To runtime-verify: (1) PartnerApp: `cd /app/frontend && npx expo start` → log in → pull-to-refresh on home. Expect: light haptic + ~90ms soft tick + 'Updated just now' pill appearing together. Repeat ~5 times quickly — tick should replay each time via seekTo(0). (2) Customer app: `cd /app/Customer && yarn install && npx expo start` → log in → pull-to-refresh on home. Same expectations. (3) Web verification: `npx expo start --web` in either app → pull-to-refresh must NOT crash (sound skipped, haptic no-ops). (4) iOS silent-switch: tick should be muted; haptic still fires. (5) Android: tick will play even on silent mode (expected / acceptable for SDK 57 default audio category).
rca of the issue: n/a — this iteration verifies E1's new feature.
